scope: 18 selected primary works, 1971–2026; bounded review, not exhaustive

sources.title: Schnelle Multiplikation großer Zahlen
sources.statement: Two n-bit integers can be multiplied in O(n log n log log n) steps.
sources.model_assumptions: Fixed multitape Turing machine or binary logical network.
sources.caller_mapping: Historical baseline; not an asymptotic native RAM record. Original full text was not available in this review.

sources.title: Faster Integer Multiplication
sources.statement: Multiplication in n log n 2^{O(log* n)} time.
sources.model_assumptions: Multitape Turing machine; same size bound for Boolean circuits.
sources.caller_mapping: Exploit cheap roots versus costly twiddles; dropping recursion only at word-sized leaves changes the invoice, not automatically the finite paid profile.

sources.title: How Fast Can We Multiply Large Integers on an Actual Computer?
sources.statement: SS-C and Fürer multiplication take O(n) time on the log-RAM; SS-F takes O(n log log n).
sources.model_assumptions: O(log n)-bit registers with arithmetic, multiplication, division, Boolean operations, cyclic shifts, indirect access and packed IO. Depth-cost model is a separate refinement.
sources.caller_mapping: Prevents falsely advertising linear Word RAM multiplication as new. Compare to packed TM transfer #4541 under the same input ABI.

sources.title: Fast Integer Multiplication Using Modular Arithmetic
sources.authors: Anindya De; Piyush P. Kurur; Chandan Saha; Ramprasad Saptharishi
locations_read: abstract; §2.2 choosing the prime, Theorem 2.2 and Remark 2.3; §2.3 root lifting
sources.statement: N log N 2^{O(log* N)} multiplication using modular arithmetic rather than approximate complex coefficients.
sources.model_assumptions: Deterministic bit complexity; chosen multivariate dimension makes required prime search sublinear in N. Root and modulus construction are charged.
sources.caller_mapping: A modular caller must pay prime generation and root lifting. Mapping the finite Gaussian word modulo p does not supply these parts. Journal version: https://doi.org/10.1137/100811167 (2013).

sources.title: Even faster integer multiplication
sources.authors: David Harvey; Joris van der Hoeven; Grégoire Lecerf
locations_read: Theorem 1.1; §3.4 Propositions 3.7–3.8; §4 Proposition 4.1 and its packing bound
sources.statement: O(n log n 8^{log* n}) bit complexity; short DFTs reduce to cyclic integer products.
sources.model_assumptions: Multitape Turing bit complexity; explicit precision, root approximations and coefficient-size bounds. Read author manuscript dated 2015; journal publication 2016.
sources.caller_mapping: Use its compositional error method and exact 2p+r+2 coefficient fields when evaluating truncated or modular alternatives; count expanded child widths.

sources.title: Faster integer multiplication using short lattice vectors
sources.authors: David Harvey; Joris van der Hoeven
locations_read: Theorem 1.1; Introduction discussion of three expansion factors; §2 overview
sources.statement: Unconditional O(n log n 4^{log* n}) multiplication.
sources.model_assumptions: Deterministic fixed finite-tape bit model; Minkowski short-vector representation plus paid conversions. Published Open Book Series 2019.
sources.caller_mapping: A representation change can improve an expansion factor only when conversion frequency is controlled. Not a free replacement for current physical entrance/exit charts.

sources.title: Integer multiplication in time O(n log n)
sources.authors: David Harvey; Joris van der Hoeven
sources.statement: O(n log n) multiplication using Gaussian resampling and multidimensional power-of-two complex DFTs.
sources.model_assumptions: Multitape Turing machine and ordinary binary encoding.
sources.caller_mapping: The current manuscript builds on this analytic reduction. A finite-field port of a dyadic network does not transport its analytic resampling estimates. Full PDF fetch failed here; no full-proof read claimed.

sources.title: Cache-oblivious algorithms
sources.authors: Matteo Frigo; Charles E. Leiserson; Harald Prokop; Sridhar Ramachandran
locations_read: 2012 journal revision abstract; §3 matrix transpose, recurrence (8), Theorem 3.2; six-step FFT work/data-movement derivation
sources.statement: Recursive transpose has O(mn) work and O(1+mn/B) misses; FFT has O(n log n) work and O(1+(n/B)(1+log_M n)) misses.
sources.model_assumptions: Ideal cache of M items and lines B with tall cache M = Ω(B²); cache misses are separate from RAM work.
sources.caller_mapping: Improve native locality and workspace scheduling; this alone leaves paid Gaussian calls and the Word RAM exponent unchanged. Source is the 2012 revision of FOCS 1999, DOI 10.1145/2071379.2071383.

sources.title: FFTs in External or Hierarchical Memory
sources.statement: Ordered transforms can use as few as two external passes under the stated hierarchical-memory layout.
sources.model_assumptions: External memory transfers, unit stride and available main-memory subtransforms; not a claim of two arithmetic passes total.
sources.caller_mapping: Reorder current monomial passes/transpose blocks for bandwidth, retaining all twiddle and arithmetic costs.

sources.title: The Truncated Fourier Transform and Applications
locations_read: abstract; univariate TFT construction; §5 multivariate statement inspected only
sources.statement: Truncated transforms smooth power-of-two jumps in polynomial multiplication.
sources.model_assumptions: Suitable roots of unity and declared input/output support. Author abstract warns of a multivariate mistake corrected in follow-up work.
sources.caller_mapping: Use only the univariate zero-tail interface here. Do not claim the older multivariate logarithmic gain without its correction or discard arbitrary dirty channels.

sources.title: A cache-friendly truncated FFT
sources.statement: Cache-friendly TFT and ITFT reorder butterfly work while preserving truncated transforms.
sources.model_assumptions: Commutative ring with invertible 2 and principal power-of-two roots; mixed Fourier/time-domain ITFT input convention.
sources.caller_mapping: Explicitly retain n transformed coordinates and complementary supplied coefficients; exact test checks the zero-tail specialization, not arbitrary dirty erasure.

sources.title: An in-place truncated Fourier transform and applications to polynomial multiplication
locations_read: §1.3; §2.1 computational model; §3 Algorithm 1 and butterfly identities
sources.statement: TFT and inverse in O(n log n) ring operations with O(1) auxiliary ring cells/pointers.
sources.model_assumptions: Input overwrite is allowed for in-place transforms; polynomial multiplication uses read-only input and read/write output; ring elements are abstract unit-cost objects.
sources.caller_mapping: Replace scratch fields only with an actual ownership-preserving schedule. O(1) ring cells need not be O(1) bits, and root generation is part of the algorithm.

sources.title: Faster polynomial multiplication via multipoint Kronecker substitution
locations_read: §1 four smaller multiplications; §3.2 reciprocal-point carry equations (4)–(8)
sources.statement: Multiple packing points reduce zero-padding and improve moderate-size polynomial multiplication constants.
sources.model_assumptions: Integer/carry recovery must reconstruct every coefficient; benefit depends on M(b) versus several M(b/k), plus linear conversion.
sources.caller_mapping: Evaluate actual child widths and conversion, not simply number of products; current signed packing already pays coefficient growth. Preprint 2007, journal 2009.

sources.title: Faster arithmetic for number-theoretic transforms
locations_read: Algorithm 4 and Theorem 3, §4, manuscript p. 6; §3 redundant ranges
sources.statement: Redundant representatives reduce modular reductions in word-prime NTT butterflies.
sources.model_assumptions: For Algorithm 4: word base β, p < β/4, inputs in [0,4p), precomputed twiddle W and quotient approximation floor(Wβ/p), high/low product access.
sources.caller_mapping: Exact exhaustive test covers input/output range and residue. This is a constant-factor native kernel optimization; it is not evidence of fewer recursive Gaussian jobs. Journal 2014.

sources.title: Broadword Implementation of Rank/Select Queries
sources.statement: SWAR operations implement practical rank/select primitives by simultaneous word-lane operations.
sources.model_assumptions: Fixed-width word arithmetic/bitwise primitives with explicit lane masks and carry discipline; author PDF updated 2023.
sources.caller_mapping: Use for address/phase metadata and safe lane arithmetic. Full-precision Θ(log n)-bit coefficients occupy only O(1) lanes in a C log n-bit word.

sources.title: Faster integer multiplication using plain vanilla FFT primes
sources.authors: David Harvey; Joris van der Hoeven
sources.statement: O(n log n 4^{log* n}) under a conjectural bound for the least prime in an arithmetic progression.
sources.model_assumptions: Conditional deterministic bit-complexity result; special FFT-prime availability must not be assumed unconditionally.
sources.caller_mapping: A word-prime CRT route needs its own unconditional or explicitly conditional prime/root supplier. No use as a proved current caller component.

sources.title: Faster integer and polynomial multiplication using cyclotomic coefficient rings
sources.authors: David Harvey; Joris van der Hoeven
locations_read: Theorems 1.1–1.2; §1.3 CRT/two-level overview; §2.2 principal roots; Proposition 3.4 construction inspected
sources.statement: Integer bound O(n log n (4√2)^{log* n}); polynomial expansion constant 4 through cyclotomic coefficient rings.
sources.model_assumptions: Deterministic bit model; coefficient ring may be a product of fields; principal roots and conversions are constructed.
sources.caller_mapping: Amortizing zero-padding across two recursion levels can change a real expansion factor. Preserve principal-root orthogonality in rings with zero divisors and charge CRT conversion.

sources.title: Integer multiplication below n log n
locations_read: 00-introduction.tex: two tape operations and exact product; 05-layers.tex: phase identities and explicit guard bound; 06-transforms.tex: signed-ring-product proof; 07-resampling.tex: one-dimensional interface
sources.statement: The pinned manuscript states T(n)=O(n (lg n)^{1−2^(−182)}) for one fixed finite-tape exact multiplier.
sources.model_assumptions: Research manuscript, not independently re-proved here; complete finite networks, source/sink frames, dyadic precision, CRT layouts and final rounding are obligations.
sources.caller_mapping: Current benchmark context. It already uses packed selected bits and signed Kronecker recovery; our new test cannot count them as newly introduced mechanisms. Modular base change applies to finite dyadic identities, not automatically to analytic resampling.
